title: ARPA-H to expedite clinical trials with SURPASS and other AI related programs
key_facts: ARPA-H, the US Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, launched the SURPASS program on 30 Sep 2026.
SURPASS stands for Simulation-augmented, Real-time Platform Adaptive Seamless Trials.
It aims to build perpetual adaptive platform trials combining predictive computational models, shared infrastructure, common control groups and real-time analysis.
ARPA-H announced three complementary projects alongside it.
Program application summaries are due 30 Nov 2026; an informational webinar is on 15 Oct and a Proposer's Day on 6 Nov.
The law firm links the effort to HHS plans such as 'Operation TrialBlazer' and to concern about China's rise in biotech.
FDA separately announced a real-time clinical trials pilot letting reviewers see data as it is collected.
quote_evidence: The program aims to build perpetual, adaptive platform trials that combine predictive computational models, shared trial infrastructure, common control groups, and real-time analysis.
why_it_matters_hint: A US health agency is funding a new approach meant to shorten clinical trial timelines using AI and shared trial infrastructure.
notes: Secondary source: a law firm's client alert summarising the ARPA-H announcement. The three complementary projects' details were not in the text we received. Event before 6 Oct, so score lowered by 1.
